title: R(k,S) as a Regime Response Surface in Energy-Flow Cosmology
description: Introduces a state-dependent gravitational response surface R(k,S) that extends EFC phenomenology from time/redshift dependence to dependence on a structural maturity variable S. The paper unifies prior µ(a) and µ(k,z) approaches, defines S operationally from the nonlinear-to-linear variance ratio, and formulates a falsifiable framework where a single global surface must describe all late-universe probes. It specifies DES Y6-oriented falsification criteria and posits that the L1→L2 transition explains the S8 tension.

transition_estimator_DeltaF.description: Regime-dependent transition strength integrating deviations from GR over the observational sensitivity window.

modified_Poisson.description: Operational closure for EFC in standard perturbation theory; µ modifies the effective gravitational coupling in the Poisson equation.

state_variable_S_def.description: Structural maturity variable measuring accumulated nonlinear structure relative to linear theory at scale R8.

S_operational.description: Operational form for S using growth factors and the conventional σ8 normalization.

mu_response_surface.description: Defines the regime response surface R(k,S) as deviations of the effective gravitational coupling from GR.

R_Taylor_expansion.latex: R(k,S) = R_0\,\Big[ 1 + a\,\ln\!\left(\frac{k}{k_0}\right) + b\,(S - S_0) + c\,\ln\!\left(\frac{k}{k_0}\right)(S - S_0) \Big]
R_Taylor_expansion.description: Local first-order phenomenological expansion of the response surface around a reference point (k0,S0), capturing scale, state, and interaction terms.

key_results.main_finding: A single, structure-dependent response surface R(k,S) with µ≈1 at S≈0 and µ>1 for S>0 can unify late-universe gravitational deviations and attributes the S8 tension to the L1→L2 transition rather than probe-specific systematics.

sealed_predictions.statement: Tomographic bins of DES Y6 3×2pt mapped to S(z) can be jointly fit by a single smooth R(k,S) surface (shared {R0,a,b,c}) without probe- or bin-specific µ.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: A joint µ(k,S) analysis of DES Y6 showing that no single parameter set fits all tomographic bins simultaneously within acceptable goodness-of-fit.

sealed_predictions.statement: Probes that sample overlapping (k,S) regions (e.g., weak lensing and RSD) will infer the same sign of deviation R(k,S) across those overlaps.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Observations where lensing prefers µ<1 while RSD prefers µ>1 (or vice versa) over the same (k,S) ranges after consistent systematics treatment.

sealed_predictions.statement: The redshift evolution of the S8 offset follows the predicted S-gradient: as S increases with decreasing z, the inferred deviation remains consistent with the same R(k,S) surface.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic S8(z) measurements whose trend with S cannot be accommodated by any smooth R(k,S) consistent with other probes.

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB-era (S≈0) observables require R(k,S≈0)≈0, i.e., µ≈1 at recombination.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Robust CMB analyses indicating statistically significant µ≠1 at recombination beyond allowed early-universe bounds.

kill_criteria: KC1: Tomographic inconsistency—if DES Y6 3×2pt redshift bins cannot be fit by a single R(k,S) surface (shared {R0,a,b,c}) within joint constraints, the framework is falsified.

KC2: Opposite-sign trend—if two late-universe probes sampling the same (k,S) region require opposite signs of R (one µ>1, another µ<1) after harmonized systematics, the single-surface hypothesis fails.
KC3: S-gradient failure—if the measured redshift evolution of S8 cannot be reconciled with any monotonic S-driven response consistent with other probes, the S-controlled response is invalidated.
KC4: Early-universe violation—if CMB data demand µ≠1 (R≠0) at S≈0 at high significance, the regime separation (L1 with GR) is ruled out.

related_packages.role: foundation: operational µ(k,z) closure for lensing

subtitle: A Unified Framework for Structure-Dependent Gravitational Response

concepts.R_k_S: Regime response function encoding gravitational deviation from GR as function of scale k and structural state S
concepts.S_state_variable: Structural maturity parameter measuring nonlinear structure accumulation
concepts.L1_regime: CMB epoch with S≈0 and μ≈1 (standard GR)
concepts.L2_regime: Late universe with S>0 and μ>1 (enhanced growth)

falsification_criteria: Tomographic consistency: All redshift bins must follow single R(k,S) surface
Trend sign matching: Probes with overlapping (k,S) must show same deviation sign
S-gradient prediction: Predicted S8 offset must match observed redshift evolution
